what_is_attested: Spelling only. 34 runes (25 single, 9 two-letter). Game audio exists but is not in the data. One wiki note says Alduin pronounces the j of Vuljotnaak as in 'Jon' while Bromjunaar has the sound of 'jarl' (Skyrim:Vuljotnaak). One wiki note says the voice acting of Throw Voice suggests Vun, not Zul (Skyrim:Throw Voice).
what_is_missing: Any official sound value. Quality and length of a / aa / ah; whether h after a vowel is sounded; values of q, x, j, r, oo, ei versus ey, ae, au, ng; a phoneme inventory.

what_is_attested: Nothing in text. Developer statement that a lone shout word is exhaled and the first word of a longer shout inhaled (Bethesda article, semi-canon).
what_is_missing: Word stress, phrase intonation, question intonation, vowel reduction, the metre of songs.

what_is_attested: Only inside u'u, in 5 dictionary spellings (Thu'um, Su'um, Zu'u, Du'ul, Strundu'ul). Rune text has no apostrophe sign (0 in 1,138 rune-case tokens); the word is written with the UU rune.
what_is_missing: Its sound (glottal stop, hiatus or length); whether new words may contain it; whether u'u and uu contrast.

what_is_attested: aa is one rune in 196 of 196 cases; ah is one rune in 225 of 240 and split A+H in 15 (shout word SAH of Phantom Form); ii takes precedence over ir (Viir = V II R); th and sh have no rune; 13 hyphens appear in rune-case transcriptions; rune text has one case and no punctuation.
what_is_missing: A rule for when ah, ir, ur are split; whether the hyphen is a rune-text sign; punctuation, word dividers and numerals in the script; rune shapes (not in the data at all).

what_is_attested: Gein 'one' (3 tokens), Ont 'once', Ney 'both', Saraan 'first' beside 'awaits'.
what_is_missing: Every cardinal from two up, ordinals, the base of the number system, fractions, the syntax of counting (plural after a numeral or not).

what_is_attested: Subject: zu'u I (23), hi you (4), rok he (13), rek she (7), nii it (3), mu we (8), nust they (3). Object: hi, nii, niin them (1; dictionary cites only the Imperial Library list). Reflexive: nimaar itself, geinmaar oneself. Fused: losei 'you are' (1).
what_is_missing: Object forms for I, he, she, we (no 'me' or 'us' word; the wiki's translations supply 'me' with no dragon word behind it); second person plural; any dual or polite form; reflexives for other persons; reciprocal.

what_is_attested: Free words: dii my/mine (10), hin/him your (21), ok his (22), ek her (4), un our (1). Suffixes: -i (10 types, all glossed 'my' in dialogue), -ii (8 corpus types plus briinahii, all third person on word walls), -iil (zaamiil 'your slave', 1), -il (bormahil, 1), -u 'our' (2 types). Juxtaposition for English 's (Alduin jot, zindro zaan). The wiki's rule: + i for my/your/his/her, + l after ii, + u for our.
what_is_missing: Which strategy applies when; the person value of each suffix (the wiki rule and the corpus disagree); 'their' and 'its'; possession by a noun (do, se or juxtaposition); suffix on plural nouns; suffix after a vowel-final stem.

what_is_attested: Double the last letter and add e: 14 corpus types (sille, meyye, drogge, dovahhe ...) plus kelle and joorre. Exceptions: hinde, bruniike (no doubling). Suppletive or collective: mun/muz, jul, dov. Plural often unmarked on walls and in the song (kendov 'warriors', jun 'kings', kul 'sons', hokoron 'enemies').
what_is_missing: Whether marking is obligatory; plural of words ending in a vowel or a two-letter rune (the rule doubles a letter, not a rune: dovah-he); plural after quantifiers; plural of compounds (inside: junne-se-jer, gaaffe-se-jul).

what_is_attested: A bare verb can be read in any tense (developer statement; mah 'fall/fell', siiv 'find/found'). fen 'will' (16), fent 'shall' (4). lost + verb or lost + verb-aan for the perfect (Zu'u lost daal; Zu'u lost kriaan hi). drey 'did' (6), dreh 'do/does' (2). Suffix -aan on boaan, duaan, kriaan, mahlaan, wahlaan, pelaan. Lexical pairs funt/funta.
what_is_missing: Whether any marking is required; a simple past; progressive, pluperfect, future perfect, habitual; the shape of -aan after a vowel (bo-aan, kri-aan with a vowel dropped, mah-l-aan with l inserted); sequence of tenses.

what_is_attested: aal 'may' (3), nis 'cannot' (2), fent 'shall'. Bare-verb imperative.
what_is_missing: can, must, should, would, could, might, want to; conditional and counterfactual; the word 'if'; hortative 'let us'.

what_is_attested: Five question marks in all dialogue. Wo meyz wah dii vul junaar? (subject who-question). Ful, losei Dovahkiin? (statement order). Boaan tiid vokriiha suleyksejun kruziik? (verb form first). Wo 'who', wen 'whose', kolos 'in which'.
what_is_missing: A rule for yes/no questions; words for what, where, why, how, which, how many, when as a question; a question particle; indirect questions; how to answer (geh 'yes' rests on the Prima guide alone).

what_is_attested: ni before the predicate (Zu'u ni faas), after an auxiliary (drey ni viik, fent ni filok), after the verb in wall imperatives (faas ni, lo ni), once with dreh (Dreh ni nahkip). nid/niid 'no' before a noun (9), neh 'never' (1), nis 'cannot' (2), prefixes ni- (4 types) and vo- (11 types).
what_is_missing: One placement rule; the negative imperative; nothing, nobody, nowhere; whether two negatives cancel; when to use ni- and when vo-.

what_is_attested: los 'is' (37), kos 'be/are' (8, after fen and once as a main verb in the song), lost 'was' (9), and no copula at all (Zu'u Alduin; Nu hin sil dii; Mu ni meyye).
what_is_missing: When the copula may be left out; los versus kos; forms by person (losei stands alone); 'there is'; becoming versus being (meyz).

what_is_attested: fin 'the' (31), faal 'the' (9, the dictionary calls it less common), aan 'a' (6), daar 'this/these' (16), tol 'that' (3). In 64 wall translations the wiki supplies 111 bracketed determiners (the 76, this 26, a 9).
what_is_missing: When an article is required; faal versus fin; 'those'; 'some' in the plural; articles with names and epithets.

what_is_attested: zok or zol 'most' + adjective (zok sahrot do naan); Zol mul glossed 'stronger'; a bare adjective read as superlative (norok 'fiercest'); ol ... ol 'as ... as' once (ww-elemental-fury-1).
what_is_missing: 'more', 'than', 'less', 'least', 'too', 'enough'; whether zok is comparative, superlative or both.

what_is_attested: wo 'who' (24) and wen 'whose' (18) after the noun; tol 'that' as complementiser once in the song; kolos 'in which' once.
what_is_missing: A relative word for things; relatives on an object or after a preposition; clauses of place and time; reported speech.

what_is_attested: ahrk and, uv or, nuz but, ol as, fod and rul when, fah for, ful so, ruz then, erei until, mindin after, med like.
what_is_missing: if, because, although, while, unless, whether, so that, either/neither, before (in time).

what_is_attested: do of/about (82, the most frequent word), se of (10, mostly inside compounds), ko in, wah to, nau and au on, ahst at, naal by, nol from, voth with, fah for, zeim through, kotin into, us before (in space), tum down, kosil within.
what_is_missing: without, under, over, between, against, behind, near, around, across, toward, among, during, since, out of, up; do versus se; au versus nau; the wiki's unexplained remark that voth 'should be avoided'.

what_is_attested: Subject, auxiliary, verb, object; adjective before noun; prepositions; relative clause after the noun. Fronted phrases only in the song, where the English lyric fronts them too. Subject left out in threats (Fen du hin sille).
what_is_missing: Whether fronting is free; adverb placement; when a subject or object pronoun may be dropped; the press claim that prepositional phrases come earlier is not borne out by the six aligned texts.

what_is_attested: Bare verb (Krii daar joorre; Aav uv dir; Dahmaan daar rot). Vocative first or last (Dovahkiin, hin kah ...). aal 'may'.
what_is_missing: First-person plural and third-person commands; polite requests; a word for 'please'.

what_is_attested: los + verb (los vahriin 'is sworn', los nahlot 'is silenced'); fen kos + verb (fen kos duaan 'will be devoured'); -aan forms as participles (mahlaan drogge 'fallen lords'); a bare verb as a noun (niid koraav 'no seeing').
what_is_missing: How the agent is expressed; a present participle; a regular way to make a verbal noun.

what_is_attested: vo- 'opposite' (11 secure types, with a variant von-), ni- 'not' (4), -maar '-hood, -self' (4), -hus/-us (3), agent -iik and -iid (2 secure pairs each at most), -aan in nouns (kulaan 'prince', onikaan 'wisdom'), free conversion (mul 'strong, strength'; kron 'victory, win, conquer').
what_is_missing: Which affixes may be used on new words; vo- versus von-; any regular adverb, adjective, abstract-noun, diminutive or agent formation.

what_is_attested: Head first with the linker se (sos-se-dov 'blood of dragon', about 15 types); head last in bynames and many solid compounds (Gaaf-Kodaav 'Ghost-Bear', Dovahkiin 'dragon-born', maltiid 'little-time'). The wiki says the language is head-initial 'in most cases'.
what_is_missing: A rule for the order of parts; when se is needed; hyphen versus solid writing; a limit on length.

what_is_attested: A part of speech is stated on 15 of 657 dictionary rows. Many words are glossed as noun and verb or noun and adjective at once.
what_is_missing: The class of every other entry; whether any root may serve as noun, verb and adjective.

what_is_attested: 657 entries, strong on war, death, honour, elements, kinship. Probe by English gloss: elements 18 of 18, kin 11 of 13, colours 10 of 14.
what_is_missing: No entry glossed go, say, take, make, think, drink, sleep, walk; heart, mouth, foot, arm; bird, fish, dog; yellow, brown; hour, morning, tomorrow, yesterday; please. (A probe by exact gloss: a near-synonym may exist.)

area: Phonotactics: status of rare and absent patterns
what_is_attested: 36 word-initial onsets, 29 word-final codas, 18 nuclei. Onsets with one word each: qu, sl, sm, sp, str. Codas with one word each: ft, kt, ld, ll, lt, lz, ng, p, rk, sh. Found only in semi-canon words: onsets dw, sp; codas ft, ll, lt, lz. Vowel hiatus and doubled consonants only at morpheme joins.
what_is_missing: Whether absent clusters (tr, bl, fl, gl, pl, sk, sn, thr) are forbidden or accidental; whether single-word patterns may be reused in coinages; whether x, ei, ey, oo may begin a word and aa, oo, uu end one.

what_is_attested: Qethsegol/Quethsegol, Miiraad/Miraad, Hadrim/Hahdrim, Nid/Niid, Him/Hin, Vokri/Vokrii, Unslaad/Unahzaal, Dov/Dovah; 17 corpus tokens classed as variant or error (thuum, krongah, tiiraaz ...).
what_is_missing: A normative spelling for each, and a policy on accepting variants as input.

what_is_attested: English from the game itself in four places only (Songs of Skyrim, Dragon Language: Myth no More, Wisdom of the Flying Gods, Arngeir's rendering of the chant). 79 dialogue records have no gloss; some wiki glosses contradict the words (Zu'u ni bo nol het given as 'I will be here').
what_is_missing: An authoritative sense list per word; a ruling on each disputed reading.

what_is_attested: 392 entries cite game text; 166 rest on the Prima guide or a Bethesda article; 91 on the Imperial Library list alone; 68 dictionary spellings never occur in the corpus. Grammar words whose dictionary row cites only Prima: rek, ek, nust, un, aal, nis, geh, se, wen.
what_is_missing: A ruling on whether each tier counts as canon for the forge, and what happens when tiers conflict.

what_is_attested: Drem Yol Lok (greeting), Drem wah hi, Pruzah wundunne (farewells), krosis (regret, apology), kogaan (blessing, thanks), ruth (curse), geh (yes), address by thuri and Dovahkiin.
what_is_missing: Thanks and requests as formulas, introductions, yes/no answers, registers (dragon, priest, Nord wall style), fillers and turn-taking words.

what_is_attested: 63 shouts with words, 136 distinct words, every one a single syllable; one to three words per shout (developer statement).
what_is_missing: What relates the three words; their order; whether any word may be a word of power.

what_is_attested: 41 translated dragon names; 38 have three syllables and 3 have four; the wiki cuts each into monosyllabic words (Mir-Mul-Nir).
what_is_missing: The order and grammar of the parts; names of mortals and places.

what_is_attested: sul day, eruvos year, tiid time, jiid moon; ont once; alun ever; nu now; ruz then.
what_is_missing: Calendar terms, clock time, today/tomorrow/yesterday, age, distance and quantity expressions.

what_is_attested: The wiki prints sentence case and English punctuation in dialogue, and rune-case (DOVahKiiN) in wall text. The developers say the language has no upper and lower case.
what_is_missing: The project's own norm for capitals, punctuation, hyphens and apostrophes in Latin text.
